arms.name: Human-AI
arms.description: Custom chatbot powered by OpenAI's GPT-4o API, available during the Frisbee post-test, asking probing questions and offering perspectives without supplying direct task solutions. Copy-paste was disabled and participants were instructed to use it as a collaborative thinking tool (PDF p. 4, Section 3.2).

arms.name: Human-Search
arms.description: Custom text-only web-search engine available during the Frisbee post-test for inspiration; visual stimuli were removed and the same copy-paste restriction applied (PDF p. 4, Section 3.2).

estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: An LLM-based automated system, citing Organisciak et al. (2023), scores novelty, usefulness, and divergence from typical applications and produces a composite creativity score. The exact scoring model/version, score scale, and rule for aggregating multiple uses into the participant score are not stated. This is automated scoring, despite the label Creativity Rating in the mediation table. See PDF p. 4 (printed p. 98), Section 3.3, continuing on PDF p. 5 (printed p. 99).
estimates.outcome: Post-test composite creativity on Frisbee alternative uses (unadjusted)

estimates.notes: Table 2 supplies participant-level post-test means and SDs. Its source quotes reproduce the complete rows in the order n, pre-test M, pre-test SD, post-test M, post-test SD, adjusted post-test M [95% CI]; only the unadjusted post-test cells are used here. Table 1 also prints the zero-order correlation between randomized condition and post-test creativity, retained as the reported r in paper_effect; condition coding is Human-Search = 0 and Human-AI = 1 (PDF p. 5, Section 3.4). The three asterisks are retained in the quote, but Table 1 has no significance legend, so no numerical p-value is assigned to that correlation. No unadjusted difference, two-arm test statistic, or contrast confidence interval is printed. The participant is the analysis unit: Table 2 uses participant counts, and the Figure 1 description identifies individual participant trajectories (PDF p. 5, Section 4). No values were read from the plotted heights, trajectories, box plots, or error bars in Figure 1. The ANCOVA below is a separate analysis of the same sample and outcome, not an independent replication.

estimates.notes: ANCOVA controls for pre-test creativity, age, work experience, gender, and race (PDF p. 5, Sections 3.4 and 4). No post-treatment mediator enters this main-effect analysis. The structured arm means, SEs, and treatment-mean CI transcribe the explicit labels in the results prose; Table 2 reverses the adjusted arm means and their CIs, as shown by the complete table rows quoted in the unadjusted record. This conflict is unresolved, and the prose labels are not a verified correction to Table 2. Figure 1 is directionally consistent with the prose, but no numeric values were estimated from it. The source quote for the control mean additionally gives the Human-Search 95% CI [2.95, 3.04]; the main ci_* fields hold only the Human-AI mean interval, not an interval for the difference. The ANCOVA test source also reports partial eta squared, printed as η²p = .166. This is retained here because paper_effect holds the separately printed Cohen's d. The paper does not state the standardizer for d, an SE or CI for d, or an SE or CI for the adjusted mean difference. No unadjusted SD is inserted into this adjusted record. The paper reports both analyses for the same outcome and sample; they must not be treated as independent estimates.

not_extracted.what: S1: self-reported ideation at pre-test and post-test, including the condition-to-ideation path
not_extracted.reason: Self-report on an adapted Runco Ideational Behavior Scale, not a score on the generated uses. It is not output-based fluency. See PDF p. 5 (printed p. 99), Section 3.3 and Table 1; PDF p. 6 (printed p. 100), Section 4 and Table 3.
A self-reported belief measured before the task and treatment, not output creativity. See PDF p. 4 (printed p. 98), Section 3.2; PDF p. 5 (printed p. 99), Section 3.3 and Table 1.

not_extracted.what: S1: open-ended self-reports of how the technological tool was used
not_extracted.reason: Self-reported confirmation of condition assignment, not a creativity or diversity score on task output. See PDF p. 4 (printed p. 98), Section 3.2.

not_extracted.what: S1: baseline fork creativity and within-condition pre-test/post-test changes
not_extracted.reason: The fork output was produced before assignment and AI access. Time and task order were fixed, so this is not a randomized-order crossover and the baseline cannot be coded as after_ai. The methods mention paired tests, but no paired-test statistics are printed. See PDF p. 4 (printed p. 98), Sections 3.1-3.2; PDF p. 5 (printed p. 99), Section 3.4 and Table 1; PDF p. 6 (printed p. 100), Table 2 and Figure 1.

not_extracted.what: S1: direct condition effect on post-test creativity in the mediation/path model
not_extracted.reason: The direct effect controls for post-test ideation, a post-treatment mediator, and is excluded under extraction rule 5. The eligible total ANCOVA contrast is recorded separately. See PDF p. 6 (printed p. 100), Section 4 and Table 3, Creativity Rating outcome, Condition row.

not_extracted.what: S1: indirect effect of condition on creativity through ideation and the ideation-to-creativity path
not_extracted.reason: Mediation and mediator-path estimates are excluded, even though creativity is the dependent variable. See PDF p. 5 (printed p. 99), Section 3.4; PDF p. 6 (printed p. 100), Section 4 and Table 3.

not_extracted.what: S1: condition-by-CSE interactions, conditional indirect effects, index of moderated mediation, and high-minus-low conditional indirect-effect difference
not_extracted.reason: Moderation and conditional mediation analyses, not full-sample total treatment contrasts; Figure 2 additionally concerns self-reported ideation. See PDF p. 6 (printed p. 100), Section 4 and Table 3; PDF p. 7 (printed p. 101), Table 3 note and Figure 2.

not_extracted.what: S1: combined-arm descriptives, non-treatment correlations, model-fit statistics, and covariate coefficients
not_extracted.reason: These are not AI-versus-comparison contrasts. Table 1's correlation between randomized condition and post-test creativity is retained in the unadjusted estimate; baseline and other correlations are excluded. Overall model fit and non-condition path coefficients do not measure the randomized contrast. See PDF p. 5 (printed p. 99), Table 1 and Section 4; PDF p. 6 (printed p. 100), Section 4 and Table 3.

open_items: Adjusted arm labels remain contradictory between PDF p. 5 (printed p. 99), Section 4, and PDF p. 6 (printed p. 100), Table 2. The adjusted estimate explicitly transcribes the prose; the table labels have not been corrected or adjudicated.

The paper reports recruitment and exclusions but not initial randomized counts separately, or arm-specific exclusions. Study and arm n_randomized remain null; analyzed counts come from the stated final sample (PDF p. 4, Section 3.1).

Exact scoring model/version, composite scale, and aggregation of individual uses into a participant score are unspecified (PDF pp. 4-5, Section 3.3). No separate output-scored novelty, usefulness, fluency, or divergence outcome is reported.
The standardizer for the printed Cohen's d and its uncertainty are not stated; no SE or confidence interval for the adjusted mean difference is printed (PDF p. 5, Sections 3.4 and 4).

GPT-4o is named, but its release year, exact model snapshot, and the chatbot system prompt are not given. The AI-tool year is therefore null rather than inferred from external information (PDF p. 4, Section 3.2).
Table 1 prints significance asterisks without its own legend. The unadjusted correlation is transcribed, but its numerical p-value is left null rather than importing the separate Table 3 legend.
notes: Extraction B, 2026-10-11. Read the entire markdown conversion through the references and extracted text from every PDF page with PyMuPDF. Examined the embedded images for Tables 1-2 and Figures 1-2 directly in memory; PyMuPDF text extraction and find_tables do not expose the cells of Tables 1-2 because those tables are images. Recovered Table 3 with find_tables. Table-image quotes are visual transcriptions of printed cells, not values estimated from figures. No appendix, embedded attachment, or separate supplement was found on file or referenced in the paper. The eligible statistic inventory comprises unadjusted arm means/SDs, analyzed participant counts, the condition-post-test correlation, and the ANCOVA arm means/SEs/mean CIs, adjusted difference, F test/degrees of freedom/p bound, partial eta squared, and Cohen's d. The two arm-mean CIs and partial eta squared are retained in the ANCOVA source quotes and notes where the single-CI/single-effect schema cannot hold all summaries at once. No statistics were calculated, transformed, or digitized. This is one between-person randomized comparison with a pre-treatment baseline, not a randomized-order within-person design. The assigned aid was available during the scored post-test. There is no across_people or after_ai outcome. No shared sample is identified in the paper or reconciled screening map; absence of overlap is not established. Initial randomized counts remain distinct from analyzed counts. H1 targets composite creativity, but no preregistered primary outcome is stated.
